# Triage brief — 2501.12934 — Correctness Assessment of Code Generated by Large Language Models Using Internal Representations (OPENIA)

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12934
Triaged: 2026-04-29

## Refutations

1. **Refutes F-2 (Prefill L19 DoM > final-token DoM) generalized beyond Qwen-2.5+MATH-500.**
   *Mechanism*: OPENIA's headline single-token probe is the **last code token at the last layer**, justified as "encapsulates the accumulated context and semantics of the entire generated sequence." Across DeepSeek-Coder 1.3B/6.7B, CodeLlama 7B/13B, Magicoder 7B and three benchmarks, this last-token / last-layer signal achieves cross-task accuracies of 0.73–0.79 — clearly above all baselines, and strictly *better* than first/early-token variants at the chosen depth. If F-2's "prefill > final" were domain-general (information about correctness lives in the prompt-side state regardless of decoding stage), OPENIA's data should show last-code-token at depth losing to first-prompt-token at depth — it doesn't.
   *Falsifiable experiment*: Take Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500 cached NPZs from `pathway11_h100/`, train OPENIA-style 128/64 MLP on (a) last-code-token at last layer (L27 for Qwen-2.5-1.5B), (b) prefill-last-token at L19. If (a) ≥ (b), F-2 is a layer-or-task-specific oddity and the prefill story is overstated.

2. **Refutes F-3 (cos(prefill_DoM, final_DoM) = 0.046 = orthogonal).**
   *Mechanism*: OPENIA's Section 5.2.2 finding is that "the deeper the layer, the more stable OPENIA's performance is across the internal representations from different tokens." At the last layer, F1 across {first token, last token, first code token, last code token} is tightly clustered (e.g. 0.74–0.78 for Magicoder on independent-unit). For F1 to remain stable across token positions, the correctness-axis at deep layers must be approximately *token-invariant* — i.e., the projection of any token's hidden state onto the probe direction is similar. F-3's near-orthogonality (cos 0.046) at L19 then either (a) doesn't hold at the last layer (i.e., F-3 is a mid-depth artifact and the geometry collapses to alignment by the readout layer), or (b) is Qwen-specific.
   *Falsifiable experiment*: On Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500, compute DoM at every layer L for both first-prompt-token and final-decoded-token states; report cos(DoM_first(L), DoM_last(L)) as a function of L. If cos rises toward 1 at L≥24, F-3 is depth-local and "prefill ⊥ final" is an L19 phenomenon.

3. **Refutes H-3 (breathing replicates on code generation).**
   *Mechanism*: H-3 conjectures the temporal participation-ratio breathing observed on math-CoT will replicate on code generation. OPENIA never sees temporal/oscillatory geometry; instead, code correctness is captured by a *static* single-layer probe — and Section 5.3.4 shows the probe **saturates F1 with only 60 % of the training data**, indicating the relevant signal is low-dimensional and stationary. Their training-data-size curve is monotone increasing then plateau, not a sign of trajectory-dependent geometry. Furthermore, their data efficiency conflicts with the "temporal collapse-and-expand" picture our breathing/F-1/F-5 framing predicts: if breathing carried correctness information uniquely, single-layer single-token probes should leave on-the-table accuracy that a temporal probe could recover.
   *Falsifiable experiment*: Run DeepSeek-Coder 6.7B on MBPP with full hidden-state caching across all 32 layers and all generated tokens. Compute layer-wise participation ratio of correct vs incorrect trajectories. If PR is flat (no breathing) and the asymmetric-collapse F-4 signature is absent, H-3 fails on code and breathing is math-CoT-specific.

4. **Refutes the implicit assumption (in F-2, H-11, H-13) that L19 is a privileged universal layer.**
   *Mechanism*: OPENIA finds the optimal layer for correctness probing varies by 12 layers across same-size architectures: L16 for CodeLlama-7B, L20 for DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, L28 for Magicoder-7B (Section 5.2.1). If "best correctness-probing layer" is architecture-conditional and not a universal property of "two-thirds-deep transformer block," then our consistent reliance on L19 across analyses (F-2, P10 v1, P11 H100 layerwise_dom) may have been Qwen-2.5 idiosyncratic. H-11 (1.5B↔7B distillation) and H-13 (head-level attribution) implicitly assume the prefill direction at L19 in 1.5B has a corresponding direction in 7B at the same relative depth — OPENIA's wide cross-model variance is a counterargument.
   *Falsifiable experiment*: For Qwen-2.5-7B, sweep all 28 layers, retrain prefill-DoM probe at each, and compare best-layer to 1.5B's L19. If they aren't proportional (e.g. 7B peaks at L22 while 1.5B's L19 is 70 % depth and 7B's L22 is 78 %), then any cross-scale stitching needs per-model layer calibration.

## Direct connections to F-N / H-N

- **F-2** (Prefill L19 DoM AUROC 0.7731 / final-token 0.7186 on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500): OPENIA's last-code-token-last-layer F1 of 0.79 (DeepSeek-6.7B cross-task) is the closest analogue. Their probe is *final-token at last layer*; our F-2 says *prefill at L19* wins on math. The paper directly contests F-2's mechanistic universality.
- **F-8** (Selective-prediction acc 71.6 % at coverage 0.5, K=2.5 avg): OPENIA's CG² pipeline (best-of-K candidate selection guided by probe score) reports 7 % average pass@1 lift, with their filtering variant pushing test-pass rate by 6–86 % over plain generation (53 %+ on repo-level). This parallels F-8's gated-compute regime — both use a probe to allocate compute.
- **F-9** (CoE-60 redundant with single-layer L19 DoM at 1024-tok labels): OPENIA's Section 5.3.4 data-efficiency saturation at 60 % training data and Section 5.2.1 mid-layer optimum together support F-9's claim that *one well-chosen layer* captures most correctness signal — multi-layer pooling is unnecessary on code.
- **H-3** (Breathing replicates on code generation): OPENIA's domain (DeepSeek-Coder + MBPP/HumanEval/DevEval) is exactly the test bed for H-3 — but they never report any temporal geometry, only static probes. Indirect refutation; see refutation #3.
- **H-12** (Semantic-entropy probes / label-free correctness signal): OPENIA's INSIDE [39] baseline (which we have in PAPER_INDEX as 2402.03744) is a label-free internal-state hallucination-detection method that OPENIA compares against. The relative ranking informs H-12.

## Methodologies extracted

- **2-hidden-layer MLP probe over single-token hidden state** — fully-connected 128/64 head, 50 epochs, batch 32, lr 1e-3, weighted-F1 objective. *Replication cost*: ~1 minute on a small GPU per probe. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — drop-in alternative to our linear DoM probe to test whether non-linearity in the probe head moves AUROC on Qwen-2.5-1.5B.
- **Last-code-token at last layer probing** — extract `h_{L,m}` where `c_m` is the last token of the generated code segment (skipping any post-code natural-language tokens). *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached NPZs. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests refutation #1 on MATH-500.
- **Per-layer probe sweep with selection** — fit probe at every layer, report best. *Replication cost*: 30min CPU on cached `pathway11_h100/layerwise_dom`. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — already partially done; reframe through "stability across tokens at that layer" lens.
- **Per-token-position probe sweep** — fit probe at fixed depth across {first token, last token, first code token, last code token}. *Replication cost*: 1h CPU. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — directly tests refutation #2 (token invariance at deep layers).
- **CG² (Correctness-Guided Generation)** — best-of-K decoding with probe-score-weighted selection. *Replication cost*: 20min CPU on cached K=8 MATH-500 samples (we already have multi-sample data via Pathway 11). *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — direct comparator for F-8 selective-prediction.
- **Probe-as-LLM-benchmark** — Pearson correlation between probe-predicted-correct rate and pass@1 across models (their values: 0.99 / 0.73 / 0.97). *Replication cost*: 10min once per-model probes exist. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — sanity check on whether DoM-predicted accuracy tracks measured K=1 accuracy across Qwen-2.5-1.5B / 7B.
- **Cross-language generalization split** — train on N-1 languages, test on Nth. *Replication cost*: not directly applicable (we're math-only). *We'd plausibly run this*: no — no MATH multi-language analogue.
- **LLM-as-A-Judge (LLM-AJ) baseline** — both in-house and external (o4-mini) zero-shot prompted correctness judgment. *Replication cost*: o4-mini API budget ~ $20 for MATH-500. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — useful black-box ceiling for our F-8 numbers and H-12.
- **LLM-Check baseline** — Eigen-analysis of hidden states + attention-map kernels + token-level uncertainty. *Replication cost*: medium (paper [40] code). *We'd plausibly run this*: maybe — overlaps with EigenScore (PAPER_INDEX 2402.03744) and EigenTrack. Worth admitting LLM-Check to the graph if we ever write up Pathway 11 breathing.
- **Length-binning of probe F1** — bin generated outputs by token-length, report F1 per bin. *Replication cost*: 10min CPU. *We'd plausibly run this*: yes — analogous to H-15 length-band PR control.

## Approaches & framings

- **"Open-box / white-box" framing for reliability assessment** — argues code-LLMs are uniquely tractable for in-process correctness probing because every intermediate state is accessible and ground-truth correctness is *objectively decidable* via tests. Intersects our F-8 / H-12: if MATH-500 numerical-correctness is similarly decidable (which it is), our results sit in the same epistemic bucket as OPENIA's, not the noisier NLG-hallucination literature. Useful framing in any writeup.
- **Process-oriented vs output-oriented probing** — OPENIA distinguishes "probing internal states during generation" (process) from "probing the final output" (post-hoc). Maps onto our prefill-vs-final-token decomposition (F-2, F-3) but assigns different semantics: prefill ≈ "model's pre-decoding state" rather than "process-during-generation."
- **Last-code-token as universal terminal aggregator** — claim that the *last token of the generated code* (not last token of the full response) is the canonical readout. We have not separated "answer-region terminal" from "post-answer-newline" (PANL) in our analysis (cf. H-18). This is a token-selection refinement F-2 may have missed.
- **Layer-architecture conditional probe selection** — argues against fixing a single layer index; advocates per-model dynamic layer choice. Bears on our cross-scale stitching plans (H-11) and any future cross-architecture replication.

## Datasets & benchmarks

- **HumanEval** — 164 standalone Python tasks; HF accessible; canonical code benchmark. *Applicable?* yes — directly tests H-3 if we run Qwen-2.5-Coder or DeepSeek-Coder-1.3B on it with our hidden-state pipeline.
- **MBPP** — 500 standalone Python tasks; HF accessible. *Applicable?* yes — same as HumanEval, for cross-task / cross-benchmark splits.
- **DevEval** — 1,825 manually-annotated repo-level Python tasks; HF accessible; tests context-dependent generation. *Applicable?* yes, but heavy — only if H-3 needs the repo-level stress test.
- **HumanEval multi-language** — Python / JS / TS / Java / C++ / C# / PHP / Bash. *Applicable?* no (we're math-domain).
- **OPENIA dataset** (24,890 generated code units + extracted hidden states) — released at https://github.com/iSE-UET-VNU/OPENIA. *Applicable?* yes — gives us a free off-the-shelf code-domain comparison set without needing 86 hours of A6000 extraction.

## Implementation details worth capturing

- Code: https://github.com/iSE-UET-VNU/OPENIA
- DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B: 32 transformer layers, 4096 hidden dim. Best-layer = 20 (independent-unit) / 28 (repo-level).
- CodeLlama-7B: 32 layers. Best-layer = 16 (independent-unit) / 32 (repo-level).
- Magicoder-7B: 32 layers. Best-layer = 28 (both settings).
- Probe: input → 128 → 64 → 2-class softmax; 50 epochs, batch 32, lr 1e-3.
- 10 candidate solutions per task generated for training data.
- Inference: 0.6 ms per code unit on P100; total probe-training ~1 min.
- Hidden-state extraction: 86 hours on NVIDIA A6000 48 GB for 24,890 units.
- Cross-benchmark MBPP→HumanEval is **prompt-template-sensitive**: F1 drops 0.79→0.67 on DeepSeek-6.7B due to wording differences. Mitigated to 0.72 via mixed-prompt training.
- Code-length effect: F1 = 0.81 for 1–30 tok, dips to 0.66 at 51–70 tok, recovers >70 tok.
- Difficulty effect: U-shape — easy (0.75 F1) and hard (high) > medium-difficulty.

## Replicable intermediates

- **Last-token-last-layer probe on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500** (refutation #1 test): use `pathway11_h100/` cached NPZ for hidden states; need last-decoded-token at last layer L27. If layer 27 isn't cached, fall back to last cached layer. Train MLP 128/64. Compare AUROC vs F-2's 0.7731.
- **Token-invariance scan** (refutation #2 test): cached `pathway11_h100/layerwise_dom` likely has per-layer first-token and final-token DoM. Compute cos per layer; produce a curve. ~20min CPU.
- **CG² on cached K=8 MATH-500 samples**: if `pathway11_h100/prefill_gated_compute` has per-sample probe scores, sort and pick the top-1. Compare to plain K=1 accuracy 48.6 %. ~10min.
- **LLM-AJ in-house baseline** on MATH-500: prompt Qwen-2.5-1.5B / 7B with "is the following math solution correct?" zero-shot. ~30min on H100 (or local CPU at low TPS).
- **Probe-pass@1 Pearson** (sanity check): correlate per-problem prefill_DoM predicted-correct rate with measured pass@1 across our two models. ~5min on cached JSONs.

## Cross-paper signals

- **2402.03744** — INSIDE / EigenScore (Chen et al., ICLR 2024). Already in graph (CITED ONLY). OPENIA cites it as ref [39] and benchmarks its INSIDE-derivative LLM-Check (ref [40]) against. Connection: another internal-state probe that targets NLG hallucination.
- **2306.03341** — Inference-Time Intervention (Li et al., NeurIPS 2023). Already in graph (CONTRADICTED). OPENIA cites as ref [102]. Same conceptual lineage of probing-then-steering.
- **2406.12541** (LLM-Check, Sriramanan et al., NeurIPS 2024) — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Uses Eigen-analysis of hidden states + attention map kernels + token-level uncertainty as a *training-free* hallucination detector. Direct conceptual sibling of EigenScore (already in graph) and a methodological alternative to our DoM probe. Worth admitting because it gives a parameter-free baseline for F-2/F-8.
- **2306.13063** (Azaria & Mitchell, EMNLP 2023, "The internal state of an LLM knows when it's lying") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Earliest hidden-state-truthfulness probe; foundational citation for any prefill / mid-generation correctness story (F-2, H-12).
- **2406.12673** (Gottesman & Geva, "Estimating knowledge in LLMs without generating a single token") — NOT in graph; recommend admission. Argues that *first-prompt-token* hidden states alone encode answer correctness — a stronger version of our F-2 prefill claim. Highly relevant to F-2 lineage.

## Proposed HYPOTHESES.md additions

### H-94: Last-decoded-token at the last layer matches or beats prefill L19 DoM on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500
**Priority:** HIGH
**Motivated by:** 2501.12934 + F-2
**Test:** Train OPENIA-style 128/64 MLP probe on (a) last-decoded-token at last layer (L27), (b) prefill-last-token at L19 (F-2's setting), on cached `pathway11_h100/` MATH-500 NPZs. Report 5-fold AUROC for each. ~20min CPU.
**Requires:** CPU only, cached NPZs, Qwen-2.5-1.5B Stage 2 hidden states across all layers (or at minimum L19 and L27).
**Would change:** If (a) ≥ 0.7731 = (b) by >0.02, F-2's "prefill > final" is overturned for this model on this task — at minimum, "prefill > final" is a *layer-mismatched* comparison and the real question is "best layer × best token" jointly. Reframes Pathway 10's prefill/final orthogonality story (F-3) and the prefill-gated-compute pipeline (F-8). On reject (a < b by >0.02), F-2 strengthens.
**Blocks:** decisive resolution of refutation #1 above; gates H-95.

### H-95: At the last layer, the correctness direction is approximately token-invariant (cos ≥ 0.5 across token positions)
**Priority:** HIGH
**Motivated by:** 2501.12934 + F-3
**Test:** On Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500, compute DoM at every layer L for first-prompt-token and final-decoded-token states. Plot cos(DoM_first(L), DoM_last(L)) vs L. ~20min CPU on cached layerwise_dom NPZs (or 1h fresh extraction if missing).
**Requires:** CPU only, cached layerwise_dom data.
**Would change:** If cos rises monotonically and exceeds 0.5 at L≥24, F-3's near-orthogonality is layer-local: at the readout layer, prefill and final are aligned, and the L19 cos=0.046 is a mid-depth disentanglement that gets re-mixed. F-3 narrative ("prefill ⊥ final") gets a "but only at intermediate depth" caveat. On reject (cos stays near 0 at all layers), F-3 is robust and OPENIA's stable-across-tokens result is code-domain-specific.
**Blocks:** nothing.

### H-96: OPENIA-style non-linear MLP probe outperforms linear DoM by >0.02 AUROC on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500 prefill L19
**Priority:** MEDIUM
**Motivated by:** 2501.12934
**Test:** Train 128/64 MLP probe on prefill L19 hidden states; 50 epochs, batch 32, lr 1e-3; 5-fold OOF AUROC. Compare to F-2's linear DoM 0.7731. ~20min CPU.
**Requires:** CPU only, cached prefill L19 NPZ.
**Would change:** If MLP > linear by >0.02 AUROC, the prefill correctness signal is non-linearly decodable — meaning any *linear* steering intervention (H-1 per-position DoM) is a lower bound on the manipulable signal. If MLP ≈ linear, linear DoM extracts all of the readable correctness information and our linear-only framing is justified.
**Blocks:** nothing; informs H-1 ceiling.

### H-97: Best-of-K selection guided by prefill DoM probe yields ≥ 5 % pass@1 improvement on MATH-500
**Priority:** MEDIUM
**Motivated by:** 2501.12934 + F-8
**Test:** On cached K=8 MATH-500 samples (Qwen-2.5-1.5B and 7B), score each candidate by prefill-L19 DoM probe, select top-1, measure pass@1. Compare to plain K=1 sampling (48.6 % for 1.5B; 73.2 % for 7B). ~20min CPU.
**Requires:** CPU only; needs cached multi-sample MATH-500 data with per-sample prefill activations (verify availability).
**Would change:** OPENIA reports ~7 % average lift across settings. If we hit ≥ 5 %, our F-8 selective-prediction story extends to selection (not just abstention) and motivates packaging the probe as a decoder plugin. If <2 %, F-8's coverage-0.5-71.6 % framing is the binding ceiling and we should not advertise selection use cases.
**Blocks:** nothing; complements F-8.

## Proposed PAPER_INDEX.md classification

## 2501.12934 — Correctness Assessment of Code Generated by Large Language Models Using Internal Representations (OPENIA) (Bui, Vu, Nguyen, Nguyen, Vo, 2025)

**Relevance:** Trains a 2-hidden-layer MLP probe on hidden states of code LLMs (DeepSeek-Coder 1.3B/6.7B, CodeLlama 7B/13B, Magicoder 7B) to predict whether generated code passes its tests. Reports cross-task accuracy 0.73–0.79 across HumanEval / MBPP / DevEval, beating CodeBERT / CodeT5+ post-hoc classifiers and LLM-Check by up to 40 %. The headline configuration uses **last code token at last layer**; layer-sweep places the optimum in the middle-to-late layers (L16–L28 across architectures). This is the exact methodology family our F-2 / F-3 / F-8 / H-3 sit in, applied to the code-generation domain.

**Key claim we tested (in our terms):** A non-linear single-token probe over a single mid-to-late layer of a code-LLM hidden state encodes binary correctness with weighted-F1 ≥ 0.73 cross-task / ≥ 0.86 repo-level, and the *last-token-at-last-layer* is the canonical readout — contradicting our F-2 ordering of prefill > final-token. The paper also reports stability of probe performance across token positions at deep layers, which contradicts F-3's near-orthogonality of prefill and final DoM.

**Our result:** **TO TEST.** The paper's last-token / last-layer probe has not been reproduced on Qwen-2.5-1.5B MATH-500 yet. P11-FE82 (replicate on Qwen) and P11-FE83 (token-invariance scan) are the two head-to-head experiments that decide whether F-2 / F-3 generalize across domain or are math-CoT-specific. Until those run, the paper sits in TO TEST as a *high-leverage refutation candidate*.

**Related experiments:** P11-FE82, P11-FE83, P11-FE84, P11-FE85, P11-FE86; H-94, H-95, H-96, H-97; bears on F-2, F-3, F-8, F-9, H-3, H-11.

**Status:** TO TEST (HIGH priority — the refutation chain to F-2 / F-3 is direct and the cost of the cross-checks is < 2 hours of CPU on cached NPZs).

## New claims

This brief introduces no quantitative claims into narrative docs. All numbers cited (0.7731, 0.7186, 0.046, 71.6 %, 48.6 %, 73.2 %) are existing entries already validated in `validate_claims.py`. The paper's own numbers (0.73–0.79 cross-task F1, 7 % CG² lift, 0.99 / 0.73 / 0.97 Pearson) are quoted from the source and live only in this brief / proposed PAPER_INDEX entry — they don't propagate into FINDINGS or HYPOTHESES bodies, so no `validate_claims.py` update is needed at promote time.
